title: How Do You Turn a Garbage Dump Into a Park?
caption: Where does your trash actually go? 🗑️➡️🌳
style: Vertical 9:16 realistic 3D engineering cutaway illustration at the edge of a small town on a clear day: a row of houses with red roofs and a road run along the top of the frame, with green fields beside them, and a large landfill pit fills the middle of the frame. The ground in front is cut away to show a deep brown soil cross-section beneath the pit, with a light-blue band of groundwater near the bottom. Clear elevated view, natural materials, readable lighting, the main action large enough to see. No text, no labels, no arrows, no watermark.
rules: Only physically possible events: nothing rewinds, teleports, glows or appears from nowhere; materials are poured, spread, laid, dumped or drilled in by machines.
Liquids and gas obey gravity and pressure: liquid drips and flows down, gas rises.
Everything already built stays exactly in place.
The town, road, fields and houses at the top stay the same.
The camera stays still unless the motion says it moves.
A clip only shows what its motion describes; the pit's fill level, the pipes and the buildings never change unless the motion says so.

lines.text: If you dump your trash in a hole outside town, you've built a landfill.
But as soon as it rains, water soaks through the garbage and turns into a black, toxic juice.
It drips out the bottom and soaks into the ground, right into the water people drink.
So scoop the trash back out, and line the hole with thick clay and a heavy plastic sheet.
Then cover the bottom with gravel and lay pipes full of holes through it.
Now, when the trash goes back in, the juice drips into the pipes and gets pumped away to be cleaned. It's called leachate.
But loose trash blows all over town, and the seagulls move in for a buffet.
So every day, bulldozers crush the garbage flat and bury it under a layer of soil.
Now the wind has nothing to grab, and the birds have nothing to eat.
But deep inside, the rotting garbage makes methane, a gas that can catch fire and even explode.
So drill pipes down into the pile and suck the gas out.
Then, instead of wasting it, burn it in engines that make electricity.
But eventually the hole is full, and rain still soaks in from the top.
So seal it with more clay, another plastic sheet and a thick blanket of soil. This is the cap.
Now the rain runs off instead of soaking in.
Plant grass, add paths and benches, and open the gates.
That big grassy hill in your local park? It might be thirty years of garbage.
Congratulations! You've turned a dump into a park.

liner.looks: a clay layer and black plastic liner in the pit

drainage.looks: a gravel layer with perforated drainage pipes at the bottom of the pit, joined to a solid white pipe that runs up the pit's side slope and over the rim into the small green pump box at the right edge

daily cover.looks: brown soil layers between flattened layers of trash

gas wells.looks: four vertical gas pipes drilled down into the trash (stopping above the gravel), each sticking up only knee-high above the surface, all four joined by one horizontal pipe lying on the surface

engines.looks: a small engine building with a chimney and power lines beside the pit

cap.looks: the sealed cap of clay, plastic sheet and soil over the full pit

park.looks: park grass, paths and benches on top

frames.shows: A plain dug pit of bare brown dirt, with no lining, half full of loose garbage bags and trash. A garbage truck at the rim is tipping more trash in.

The same pit is now empty: all the trash has been scooped out, leaving bare brown dirt with no lining. A yellow excavator stands at the rim beside a loaded garbage truck. The darkened soil under the pit has been dug out, so the pit is slightly deeper and its floor is clean brown dirt.

Is the pit bare brown dirt: no clay, no black plastic sheet, no gravel, no pipes?
Is there a yellow excavator at the rim and a loaded truck beside it?

frames.shows: The same pit is now empty: the trash has been scooped out, and the pit's floor and walls are covered with a layer of brown-grey earthy clay, with a heavy black plastic sheet laid over the clay. The garbage truck is gone.
A layer of grey gravel now covers the bottom of the lined pit, with white pipes full of small holes running through the gravel to a pump pipe at the edge.

The lined pit now has a layer of loose trash covering the bottom third, lying on top of the gravel and pipes; the gravel, the white pipes and the liner are still visible in the cut-away below the trash. Two garbage trucks stand at the rim, their beds tipped up and empty. No plastic bags in the air, no seagulls yet.

frames.camera: it has moved down and about twice as close to the bottom of the pit, with the pipes still running left to right exactly as before
frames.shows: Trash now fills the lower part of the lined pit. Dark liquid trickles down through the trash into the gravel and into the holes of a white drainage pipe, flowing away along it.
The lined pit is one third full of loose trash. Plastic bags are blowing up out of it toward the houses, and a flock of seagulls circles and lands on the trash.

The pit is only half full: the soil top is about halfway down, and the black liner wall shows clearly above it all the way round. Its ENTIRE top surface is now a smooth, flat layer of brown soil: no trash is visible anywhere on the surface, no plastic bags, no seagulls. A yellow bulldozer, small compared to the pit, is smoothing the last strip of soil at one corner. In the cut-away front of the pit the layers are clearly visible: flattened trash, then a band of brown soil, then flattened trash, then soil on top, like a layered cake, resting on the gravel and drainage pipes at the bottom.

frames.shows: Same pit, same fill level and same smooth brown soil top as before; the bulldozer has gone. Added: four white gas pipes drilled straight down through the soil into the trash, in a row from left to right. Each pipe stops inside the trash, well above the gravel, and sticks up only knee-high above the soil. One horizontal white pipe lies on top of the soil and connects to the top of ALL FOUR pipes, the leftmost included, then runs to the right edge of the pit. In the cut-away, the pipes are seen going down through the layers of trash and soil. Clean sharp image, same quality as the reference.

frames.shows: Everything as before (pit half full, smooth soil top, the four vertical gas pipes and the horizontal pipe). Added: at the right edge of the pit, a small grey engine building with a short chimney, connected to the horizontal gas pipe, and a line of power poles with wires running from it toward the houses.

The four gas pipes have been extended up to this new surface and still join the horizontal pipe to the small engine building at the right edge, with its power lines to the town. Rain is falling, and in the cross-section dark wet streaks soak down from the soil top into the upper layers. The top is NOT sealed yet: no clay and no plastic sheet on top.

The four gas pipes now reach up through the cap and end in short pipe heads on the surface, still joined to the engine building at the right edge, with its power lines to the town. The layers of trash and soil and the liner and gravel at the bottom are still visible in the cross-section.

frames.camera: it has pulled back to show the whole mound and more of the town around it
frames.shows: The mound is now a green park hill with grass, winding paths, wooden benches and a few young trees. An open gate at the front edge lets people in; people walk dogs and jog on the hill. The short gas pipe heads still poke out of the grass, and the small engine building with its power lines is still at the right edge. The cross-section below the hill still shows the cap, the layers of trash and soil, and the liner and gravel at the bottom.

clips.motion: The garbage truck tips its load and trash tumbles into the pit.
Rain starts falling on the pit. In the cut-away soil directly beneath the pit, black liquid begins dripping out of the bottom of the trash.
The black liquid spreads down through the cut-away soil in a dark trail and the first of it reaches the blue groundwater band, where a small dark cloud starts to spread.
An excavator at the rim scoops the trash, together with the darkened soil just under it, back out of the pit and loads it into two trucks waiting beside the pit, until the pit is empty bare dirt.
A grey clay layer and then a black plastic sheet are spread over the empty pit's floor and walls.
Gravel pours over the bottom of the lined pit and white pipes full of holes are laid through it.
The two trucks tip the trash back into the lined pit, on top of the gravel and pipes, until the bottom third is filled.
The camera moves down closer as black liquid trickles down through the trash and gravel, into the holes of the white pipe, and flows along the pipe toward the pump at the edge.
The camera pulls back to the whole pit as wind lifts plastic bags out of the loose trash and seagulls swoop in.
A bulldozer crushes the trash flat and spreads a layer of brown soil over it; the seagulls fly off.
A gust of wind blows a little dust across the smooth soil but nothing lifts. One seagull lands, pecks at the bare soil, finds nothing and flies away.
A faint shimmering haze, like heat haze, rises from thin cracks in the soil, and for a moment a small flame flickers up from one crack and goes out.
A small drilling rig bores four holes down into the trash; a white pipe is lowered into each hole, and a pipe laid along the soil joins all four tops.
A small engine building is set at the edge of the pit, the gas pipe connects to it, and a little exhaust rises from its chimney.
In a quick time-lapse, more flattened layers of trash and soil build up until the pit is full to the rim, the gas pipes growing up with them; then rain falls on the flat top and soaks in.
Layers are spread over the full pit one after another: grey-brown clay, a black plastic sheet, and a thick blanket of brown soil, rounding it into a low mound. The gas pipes stay poking up.
Rain falls on the sealed mound and runs off down its sloped sides in little streams instead of soaking in.
Grass spreads over the mound, paths and benches appear and a few young trees grow; a gate at the front opens and people walk in as the camera pulls back.
People walk dogs and jog over the green hill while, in the cross-section below them, the buried layers of trash stay still.
Gentle hold on the park and the town as the sun lowers slightly.

tests.name: hard-shot model test (bulldozer)

tests.command: python3 -m cutaway compare landfill --models kling-o3,seedance25 --clips C08 --estimate

tests.decide: If Seedance 2.5 is clearly better at the physical action, set "model": "seedance25" on the 2-3 hardest clips only (each ~$1.30 at 720p). Otherwise keep Kling everywhere.
